title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Named public destinations along the Broadway, First Hill, Pike-Pine, and Yesler corridors near Seattle University.

cards.title: See art at the Frye
cards.subtitle: Terry Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Walk to 704 Terry Avenue and use the museum’s free admission to spend time with the exhibitions before continuing along First Hill.
cards.short_summary: A free art museum on Terry Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Frye Art Museum is at 704 Terry Avenue and states that admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Museum and store hours listed: Wednesday–Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m.

cards.title: Visit St. James Cathedral
cards.subtitle: 9th Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Use the cathedral’s directions page to locate the building at 804 9th Avenue and check its current worship or visitor information before going.
cards.short_summary: A landmark cathedral on the First Hill side of 9th Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: St. James Cathedral lists its address as 804 9th Ave., Seattle, WA 98104.
cards.access_notes: Consult the cathedral’s current schedule before a visit.

cards.title: Pause at First Hill Park
cards.subtitle: University Street corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Stop at 1201 University Street to see the custom bronze chair, ottoman, and bear-cub sculpture, then use the seating and lawn for a short break.
cards.short_summary: A compact city park with a distinctive bronze sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: First Hill Park is at 1201 University Street and features a custom bronze sculpture of an Edwardian chair, ottoman, and two bear cubs.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Walk the park above I-5
cards.subtitle: Seneca Street corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Enter at 700 Seneca Street and follow the paths through the landscaped park, which connects the First Hill edge with downtown over the freeway.
cards.short_summary: A 1976 park landscape built above Interstate 5.
cards.evidence_claim: Freeway Park is at 700 Seneca Street; the City says it was built atop a freeway and is bounded by Union, Spring, 6th, and 9th avenues.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; construction work may affect features.

cards.title: Use the Capitol Hill Branch
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Head to 425 Harvard Avenue E. for public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, study rooms, and the branch’s LGBTQ+ collection during open library hours.
cards.short_summary: A public library branch with study and technology amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Capitol Hill Branch is at 425 Harvard Ave. E. and lists study rooms, public computers, Wi-Fi, and print/copy/scan among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Capitol Hill Branch | The Seattle Public Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists daily open hours and a 24/7 book return; verify schedule changes before traveling.

cards.title: Take the park loop
cards.subtitle: 11th Avenue corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Start at 1635 11th Avenue and use the city’s listed paths, reflecting pool, promenade, lawn, and oversized chess boards for an outdoor reset.
cards.short_summary: A city park with paths, water features, lawn, and chess boards.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Anderson Park is at 1635 11th Ave. and includes promenade paths, a reflecting pool, athletic field, and oversized chess boards.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Find Seattle Central on Broadway
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor, Capitol Hill
cards.notes: Walk to the main brick Broadway–Edison Building at 1701 Broadway; check building hours and only enter areas open to the public or scheduled visitors.
cards.short_summary: Seattle Central College’s main Broadway building.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle Central College identifies the Broadway–Edison Building at 1701 Broadway as its main brick building.
cards.source_title: Directions, Maps & Parking Info | Seattle Central College
cards.access_notes: The college posts building hours separately; access can be limited outside them.

cards.entity_name: Broadway & Marion First Hill Streetcar Stop
cards.title: Board the First Hill Streetcar
cards.subtitle: Broadway corridor at Marion Street
cards.notes: Use the Broadway & Marion stop as the First Hill connection point; confirm fare and service notices with Seattle Streetcar before boarding.
cards.short_summary: A named First Hill Streetcar stop on Broadway.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle’s First Hill Streetcar stop list includes Broadway & Marion in First Hill.
cards.source_title: First Hill Line | Seattle Department of Transportation
cards.access_notes: The City lists service through 10:30 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 8 p.m. Sunday/holidays; verify service alerts and fares.

cards.title: Climb the Horiuchi Park steps
cards.subtitle: Boren Avenue corridor, First Hill
cards.notes: Find the small staircase park at 156 Boren Avenue and take in the community garden and view before continuing between First Hill and Yesler.
cards.short_summary: A stair-step pocket park named for artist C. Paul Horiuchi.
cards.evidence_claim: Horiuchi Park is at 156 Boren Ave., is named for artist C. Paul Horiuchi, and is described by the City as a small staircase with a community garden.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.

cards.title: Explore Yesler Terrace Park
cards.subtitle: Yesler Way corridor, Yesler Terrace
cards.notes: Visit the two-acre park at 917 E Yesler Way to use its plaza and walk past the sculptural installations; seasonal water features may vary.
cards.short_summary: A two-acre park with plaza, art installations, play, and sport amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Yesler Terrace Park is at 917 E Yesler Way and includes a plaza, sculptural installations, playground, basketball court, and soccer spot.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 4 a.m.–11:30 p.m.; seasonal spraypark operations are subject to conditions.
